name: Pixel layout+kernel co-design: MOSS decode ms/token on Pixel 10 Pro (#317)

description: Baseline A/B (identical binaries): base median 68.08, cand 70.0 ms/token; one 137 outlier round (thermal/slow-mode). Round spreads: base 67.67/69.25/68.08, cand 68.99/70.02/137.62. Harness validated after phone-environment battles (screen-on compositor noise, GPU device-memory degradation across loads, adb waiter self-match hang).

asi.finding: phone GPU memory degrades across repeated 1.6GB model loads (vkWaitForFences VkResult 2 = device OOM after ~6-8 loads, worse with uptime); reboot restores; decode degrades to ~137 ms/token in slow mode under sustained load+charging
asi.hypothesis: Baseline: identical base/cand binaries (master+phase0, no kernel change); validate A/B harness + noise floor
asi.measure_protocol: screen MUST be off (compositor shares GPU: 2x swings otherwise); wait for previous bench process via pidof (pgrep -f self-matches: infinite loop); reboot before long sessions if vkOOM appears; ~6 model loads per session budget

description: BASELINE: MOSS decode 75.35 vs base 77.13 ms/token on identical binaries (order-balanced A/B, 2 rounds × 6 runs, screen off, post-reboot). Noise floor ±2.5%; deltas <3% = noise; absolute numbers boot-dependent. Transcript gate ✓ (delta -2.31%).

asi.gpu_health_budget: ~8 model loads per boot; reboot when vkOOM or bench startup hangs appear
asi.hypothesis: Official baseline after harness stabilization: identical binaries, balanced ordering
asi.noise_floor: identical binaries measure +/-2.5% between sides (75.35 vs 77.13); deltas under ~3% are noise; absolute ms/token varies per boot (68-77) - only same-window A/B counts
asi.phone_protocol: reboot; screen off; kill background apps; ROUNDS=2 RUNS=6; base binary pinned by commit + base_dirty marker

description: int8-x W8 lm_head GEMV via dotPacked4x8EXT: correct (micro rel err 1e-3, transcripts identical) but NO speed win: real-shape isolated 42.5 vs 43.4 GB/s, end-to-end 73.81 vs 73.33 (+0.65%, noise). The op-issue ceiling applies equally to SDot; v1's manual x-quant (~8 ops/vec4) ate the savings.

asi.bottleneck_model: ALL vector ops (f32 FMA, SDot) share ONE ~38.5 G ops/s issue ceiling on DXT: alu probe 77.5G f32 MAC/s = idot probe 154G i8-MAC/s = 38.5G ops/s; W4 scalar ~ W8 scalar ~ 37-38 G w/s regardless of bytes -> per-weight op COUNT is the only lever; dot4 saves ops only if aux ops shrink too
asi.expected_vs_measured: expected ~7% (lm_head ~18% of decode, 2x kernel); measured isolated real-shape -2% (42.5 vs 43.4 GB/s), end-to-end +0.65% (noise)
asi.hypothesis: int8 activations on the W8 lm_head GEMV via OpSDot cut ALU per weight ~2x on the issue-bound decode
asi.next: v2: replace the 8-op-per-vec4 manual x-quant with packSnorm4x8 (1 op per 4 values) - the x-quant overhead (~0.14 ops/w amortized over RPP=16 rows) cancels the dot savings in v1
asi.overheads: per-32w budget v1: dots 0.25 + x-quant 0.14 + loads 0.1 + scale FMA 0.06 ~= scalar path; v2 target ~0.45 ops/w -> ~85 G w/s

description: Probe session: skinny GEMM flat 7.1ms M=1..16 (6.8x GEMV — speculative needs an M-token GEMV kernel, ~1.6-1.8x op cut/token at M=4-8); f16 dots 4 MAC/slot on DXT (same as SDot, 2.6x f32 FMA). GEMV plateau ~40 G w/s is structural (latency/occupancy), not op-count.

asi.f16_dot_rate: phone: 377 G f16-MAC/s = 94 G dots/s = 4 MAC/slot; f32 FMA 246 G MAC/s; i8 SDot 159 G MAC/s = 4 MAC/slot - same slot efficiency as f16
asi.gemm_skinny: phone tiled GEMM W4 6144x2048: flat 7.1-7.3ms at M=1..16 vs GEMV 1.04ms - the M rows are free but M=1 costs 6.8x a GEMV; speculative verify needs a dedicated M-token GEMV (unpack+load amortization ~1.6-1.8x fewer ops/token at M=4-8)
asi.gemv_plateau: all GEMV variants (W4 scalar/W4U/W8/W8-idot/F16) land 37-46 G w/s; probe headroom 2-4x exists in dots alone -> latency/occupancy structural limit, not op count
asi.hypothesis: Side measurements (#311 pricing + f16-dot rate): no code-path change, pure probes

description: W4_NOSCALE speed probe (scale load removed, wrong numerics by design): saturated lm_head shape unchanged (25.7 vs 26.5 GB/s) — scale stream free at saturation; small N=6144 shape +28% (load-latency dominated when unsaturated). Scale-interleave layout idea: not supported.

asi.hypothesis: The W4U GEMV plateau (~40 G w/s) comes from the second load stream (scale arena) / load-path costs; removing the scale load prices it
asi.learning: phone: N=151936 rows=32 (saturated, 4748 WGs): noscale 25.7 vs baseline 26.5 GB/s - the scale stream costs NOTHING at saturation; N=6144 rows=16 (384 WGs, unsaturated): noscale 15.0 vs 10.7 GB/s (+28%) - small-N GEMVs are latency/load dominated. Dual-stream scale-interleave layout (idea #5) has no support for the saturated case; small-N overheads are real but those shapes don't saturate the GPU in isolation anyway
asi.next: M-token GEMV kernel (the measured lever): per 32w at M=2, unpacks shared -> ~12 ops/token vs 20 at M=1 (1.67x predicted cut); build as micro-measurable variant
